title: Reduce Completed real media proof export
summary: Removed the transitional Completed real-media proof flat export while preserving mediaPipelineCompletedView.renderCompletedRealMediaProof(). Pending Publish and the Completed/Pending browser smoke now use the Completed namespace helper, backend-served/static tests guard against flat-assignment regression, and generated WebView inventory/contract artifacts report 500 flat exports.
reason: Continue namespace-first WebView cleanup in the touched Completed/Pending proof domain without changing backend ownership, media policy, pending-publish drain, filesystem mutation, or source media handling.
behavior_before: completedView.js exposed renderCompletedRealMediaProof through mediaPipelineCompletedView and as a transitional window.renderCompletedRealMediaProof flat export. Pending Publish and browser proof smoke paths still read the flat alias.
behavior_after: renderCompletedRealMediaProof remains available through mediaPipelineCompletedView only. Pending Publish and browser smoke paths use the namespace helper, the Completed/Pending browser smoke fails if the served flat assignment returns, and the documented flat-export count is 500 across 49 files.
tests_added: Extended tests/webview/test_webview_browser_completed_pending_proof_smoke.py to use the namespace helper and reject a served window.renderCompletedRealMediaProof flat assignment.
Updated tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_local_api.py to require the namespace export and reject window.renderCompletedRealMediaProof.
rollback_plan: Restore the window.renderCompletedRealMediaProof assignment in completedView.js, move the touched consumers back to the flat alias only if compatibility is intentionally required, regenerate the WebView public contract baseline and summaries, and rerun the same WebView/static validation ladder.
notes:
Source-media safety: this is a frontend compatibility-export cleanup only. It does not change backend routes, strict confirmations, repair/apply behavior, pending-publish manifests, drain behavior, filesystem mutation, source/scratch/output handling, FFmpeg arguments, or media policy. No downloads or real-media validation are required for this low-risk WebView namespace cleanup.
